video_title: JR Smith NBA Champion on being depressed 70% of his career, winning with LeBron and Knicks|The Pivot

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his versatility as a multi-sport athlete
quotes.excerpt: There are people in the world, Odell Beckham Jr. like, he could do everything.
quotes.quote: There are people in the world, Odell Beckham Jr. like, he could do everything. He could hoop, he could play soccer, he could play baseball. You the same, man. You played football, baseball, ping-pong, you could golf, all of these different things. Was it hard to sort of settle down into doing one thing because you were so good at so many?

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Clark
text_blocks.text: There are people in the world, Odell Beckham Jr. like, he could do everything. He could hoop, he could play soccer, he could play baseball. You the same, man. You played football, baseball, ping-pong, you could golf, all of these different things. Was it hard to sort of settle down into doing one thing because you were so good at so many?

text_blocks.speaker: JR Smith
text_blocks.text: Yeah, for me, it was, I was, I said, it's crazy because I still say it, but I was a football player. I consider myself a football player. Football was like the one of the sports, was actually at one point the only sport I had a scholarship in.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his early basketball development and growth spurt
quotes.excerpt: I didn't grow until what, sophomore year. My freshman year to sophomore year I grew six and a half inches.
quotes.quote: No, basketball was my, I mean I've been playing basketball since I was three. But it just so happened like I was, I wasn't, I didn't grow until what, sophomore year. My freshman year to sophomore year I grew six and a half inches. Like in the summer. It was like three months. I went from literally being able to barely dunk to putting that shit between my legs and behind my back in the air in three months like that.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the pros and cons of reclassifying in high school
quotes.excerpt: It should never have to do with the parents trying to get ahead and using their kid as leverage.
quotes.quote: I think it depending on the on the kid. Well, for one, it should never have to do with the parents trying to get ahead and using their kid as leverage to to me to to do better for them. You should only want to do better for your kids. You put yourself in that situation where where you live the way you live and you raise your kids the way you did and it just so happened that they became successful. I don't think you should put that on your kid to where it's like, I'm using my kid to essentially pay me back in a sense. That's the way I look at it.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on how tutors helped him overcome learning difficulties
quotes.excerpt: I had tutors and they literally constructed a game plan on how to study.
quotes.quote: I had tutors and they literally constructed a game plan on how to study. And we went through it every single day. Like it was like like a workout. Like you was preparing for a game or a season. And when I did that, for me, it was like, I didn't I never thought of it like that. Like it was literally broke down in increments of 30 minutes, 15 minutes, just because the way I think, I can't sit there and do the same shit over and over and over again.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his grandmother's passing and his struggle with smoking
quotes.excerpt: She died from lung cancer, ironically because I smoke all the time.
quotes.quote: She was like the matriarch of our family and at a very early age I understood that, and she died from lung cancer, ironically because I smoke all the time. She was a smoker. And at the same time that happened, they put me in these classes and my childhood started changing. I kind of disassociated myself from friends and I threw myself more into my family. My siblings, my cousins, I had a lot of cousins too growing up. It was like where we didn't I didn't live near where they lived at, but we was all from Jersey so I got like literally like 20 some cousins, we all around the same age.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his distrust of others and the impact on his life
quotes.excerpt: I feel like it was to my detriment because I don't really give people the benefit of the doubt.
quotes.quote: I feel like it was to my detriment because I don't really give people the benefit of the doubt because I don't trust them off the rip and I don't give them an opportunity to really show me who they are because I lead with this preconception of this is dangerous, this person can like affect me in a lot of ways.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the lack of support for players' mental health
quotes.excerpt: There's no way you shouldn't be able to get any kind of help mentally, physically, for anything.
quotes.quote: There's no way you shouldn't be able to get any kind of help mentally, physically, for anything. There's no way. If you need to go talk to somebody and all that, that shit should be paid for by the whole league and you ain't got to worry about nothing. Every single player who played. They don't care about players. They don't care. It's literally how many tackles did you make? How many yards you get? You know what I'm saying? But there is that, you know what I'm saying, now the mental health and all that stuff.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the toll of his career and personal struggles
quotes.excerpt: I played 16 years, I probably played 70% of my career depressed.
quotes.quote: I played 16 years, I probably played 70% of my career depressed. That's crazy to think about. That's nuts. And to still be able to have a, I would say a good career, it wasn't great, it was a good career, but I literally think about this shit all the time, bro. My potential was so high in that aspect of it.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his addiction to smoking as a coping mechanism
quotes.excerpt: I'm addicted to smoking because of a lot of the depression and pain that I feel.
quotes.quote: I'm addicted to smoking because of a lot of the depression and pain that I feel and I don't know how to get out and express it. I've been to therapy, I don't trust therapists because I don't I a lot of them tell you what you want to hear. And I've learned to where I don't, me personally, I've been around enough people to kiss my ass, I don't really need that.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his first workout with LeBron James in Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: LeBron was like Kobe at the time, like mentally, he wasn't dropping the jewels.
quotes.quote: Yeah, when I first got to the league I went to to Akron and went to workout with Bron. But Bron was like Kobe at the time, like mentally, he wasn't like he wasn't dropping the jewels and like he was going to workout but he wasn't telling me he was going. Like we would go workout once and then I come find out the next day he went worked out like three other times. I'm like, yo bro, you wasn't going to tell me? Like damn. But that's he been like that though, man. That's that I was like, that was my first introduction to like really like somebody who worked.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the 2018 NBA Finals and the decision not to call timeout
quotes.excerpt: I'm thinking we are going to call timeout. It looked like they was trying to deny Bron.
quotes.quote: I'm thinking we are going to call timeout. It looked like they was trying to deny Bron, so I'm dribbling it out to get the ball to Bron. Like bro, if I shoot this shit they going to be mad as fuck. You shoot this shit, they going to be like, well, we going to live and die with that. I'm literally looking at him like, I'm trying to get you the ball. Like bro, this is your job. This is your job. You like, that's why you get the big bucks. They don't pay me enough for this shit.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the culture built by Dwyane Wade and LeBron James in Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: I credit West and Leon on that. They really built a culture to make the players be a part.
quotes.quote: I credit West and Leon on that. They really built a culture to make the players be a part of the family even after you move on to even to a different team or to retire or whatever. And then I feel like that's the way it should be. Like you should be, you should, especially if you played in that city or played well in that city and you are a household name in that city, like you should take care of your players. Like that should be a thing.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the lack of appreciation for the Cavaliers' 2016 championship
quotes.excerpt: They've won one championship in the last how many years? That's what I'm saying.
quotes.quote: I mean they've won one championship in the last how many years? That's what I'm saying. Just saying. Like it's crazy. It's weird.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on his perspective on the 2016 NBA Finals win
quotes.excerpt: I think the 3-1 was harder because the team we was facing.
quotes.quote: I mean I think the 3-1 was harder because the team we was facing. I think the Warriors was just, I mean they was the best record in the league at the time, ever. I think that team was just probably one of the best teams that ever was assembled. But I think the bubble one was definitely hard because the consistent grind staying there and like the fans and all of that, all our dog getting tested every day, all that shit was weird. And seeing your opponent literally in the hotel, you I'm getting on the elevator, I plan against this dude in an hour, I see him on the elevator, like bro, I don't want all that.

quotes.speaker: JR Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: JR Smith on the importance of mental health and education for players
quotes.excerpt: I feel like for me, if I was capable of expressing myself and understand at an earlier age.
quotes.quote: I feel like for me, if I was capable of expressing myself and understand at an earlier age, I feel like a lot of my own thoughts wouldn't be to my detriment. And I didn't I didn't realize this until as I got older and and still even still, it's having those hard conversations, having the courage and boldness to have those tough conversations with people, you really find out that it's not that bad. It's not as bad as you think. And I didn't learn that for a long time and I feel like for me, if I was earlier on, I wish I'd have I wish I'd have had that.
